questions.q: How was the dominance of the Congress restored under Indira Gandhi by 1971?
answer: After the setback of 1967 and the split of 1969, the Congress under Indira Gandhi recovered its dominance dramatically by 1971.

answer.text: In 1969 the Congress split into the Congress (O), led by the older Syndicate leaders, and the Congress (R), led by Indira Gandhi. Freed from the control of the old guard, she projected herself as a bold, decisive leader close to the people.

Indira Gandhi adopted a strongly populist and pro-poor programme. She nationalised the major banks, abolished the privy purses of the former princes, and raised the powerful slogan of Garibi Hatao, or Remove Poverty. These steps won her the support of the poor, minorities and weaker sections.
In the 1971 general elections her Congress won a sweeping majority, and the victory in the war that created Bangladesh soon after further boosted her standing.

answer: Thus, through new leadership and populist appeal, Indira Gandhi restored Congress dominance around herself.
